change_summary: The journal published an expression of concern saying the editors have been made aware of concerns about some of the data reported in this article. The matter is still being looked into, and the notice does not say which data are in question. The paper's main reported result is the forced-swim test effect after transplanting gut bacteria from depressed donors (Figure 3), but the notice does not say whether it is affected. The findings are in doubt, not withdrawn, because the concern is about data and is unresolved.
evaluation: Your Discussion cites Lopez and Chen [8] as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, supporting a causal role of gut bacteria, and says your proposal builds on this finding. The paper's abstract reports that transplanting gut bacteria from depressed donors made recipient mice less active in a forced-swim test. The journal's expression of concern says the editors have been made aware of concerns about some of the data, but the notice does not say which data. So it is uncertain whether the result you rely on is touched. Overall the impact is medium, because this finding underpins your Discussion argument and proposal while the affected data remain unidentified.
recommendation: The journal's expression of concern says the editors have been made aware of concerns about some of the data in the article, and the notice does not say which data. Your Discussion cites Lopez and Chen [8] as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, supporting a causal role of gut bacteria, and says your proposal builds on this finding. Hedge the wording of that Discussion sentence and cite the notice. Avoid building new work on this finding until the journal resolves the concern, and consider independent supporting studies; tracking continues, so a retraction would raise a new alert.
